question: Will Turkey's Court of Cassation have issued a ruling in the CHP 'mutlak butlan' case by September 17, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status confirmed unresolved as of 2026-09-07: file at Yargıtay 3. HD since 17-20 July, preliminary review since ~26 July, substantive panel review deferred past the 20 Jul-31 Aug recess; no agenda or hearing date announced. Reference class is 'politically salient file pending before a Turkish cassation civil chamber, no scheduled date, 11-day horizon' — ordinary Yargıtay civil-chamber disposition averages ~230 days from arrival, so a ruling by 17 Sep would be at day ~62, far into the fast tail even allowing large expedition for political salience. The most recent insider reporting (Türkiye, 6 Sep) puts the expected ruling 'by November'; CHP's own operational planning (Kılıçdaroğlu's 9 Sep congress calendar, provincial/district congresses first, Grand Congress only after finalization, 18 Sep leadership meeting) is built around a ruling weeks out, and the first week of the new judicial year passed with no movement. Upside risk is real but modest: chambers decide on the papers with zero notice, the tetkik hakimi report has been ripening since late July, and this case has produced surprise timing before. Extra drag: a disposition confined to the 25 Aug appeal withdrawals (CHP HQ, Özkanat, Karaslan) would not count as a merits ruling under the fine print, and Özel's appeal keeps the merits alive. No market exists to anchor on.

HD's 21 May 2026 mutlak butlan decision, reported by AA or comparable. Does NOT resolve off: the BAM decision itself, the separate criminal case, a clerical correction, a ruling only on withdrawn appeals, or finalization by all parties withdrawing.

PROCEDURAL TIMELINE (facts):
- 21 May 2026: Ankara BAM 36. HD issues mutlak butlan on CHP's 38th Ordinary Congress (4-5 Nov 2023); interim reinstatement of Kılıçdaroğlu and pre-congress party organs (NTV, 20 Jul 2026).
- 24 Oct 2025: Ankara 42. Asliye Hukuk had earlier ruled the annulment request moot ('konusuz kalma'); BAM reversed course on istinaf (internethaber, 20 Jul 2026).
- 17 Jul 2026 (Fri): file dispatched to Yargıtay 3. HD, 56 days after the decision, one business day before the recess; registered 20 Jul (Euronews 20 Jul; Türkiye Gazetesi 20 Jul).
- 20 Jul - 31 Aug 2026: adli tatil. Lawyers quoted saying this file type is not among cases reviewable during recess (Türkiye Gazetesi).
- ~26 Jul 2026: file moved from 'kayıt' to 'ön inceleme'; tetkik hakimi to prepare a report for the panel; panel's esas review stated as expected after 1 Sep (NTV, Hürriyet, Cumhuriyet, Habertürk, samanyoluhaber, all 26 Jul).
- 25 Aug 2026: Kamile Bahar Özel, Yılmaz Özkanat, Hatip Karaslan withdraw their temyiz ('butlan kararı kesinleşsin diye'); appeals of CHP Genel Merkezi, Özgür Özel (now leader of 'YENİ Parti'), Levent Çelik and Lütfü Savaş remain live at the Yargıtay; CHP staff said withdrawal of the HQ appeal would be taken up by party organs in coming days (T24 / BirGün / Sözcü, 25 Aug).
- As of 7 Sep 2026: no announced panel agenda date, no duruşma date, no report of the tetkik hakimi report having been submitted; searched for these and found nothing.

PROCEDURAL MECHANICS: Yargıtay civil chambers commonly decide on the file ('dosya üzerinden') without a public hearing, so a disposition can surface with no advance notice. Possible dispositions named in coverage: onama; bozma with remand; bozma limited to the interim measure while leaving the congress annulment; procedural bozma without reaching the merits.

BASE RATES:
- Over all Yargıtay civil-chamber files (2025 figures cited by practitioner sources): mean time from arrival to disposition ~230 days; by chamber, 2. HD ~274, 9. HD ~312, 11. HD ~386 days; commonly quoted overall range 6 months to 1.5 years (tahanci.av.tr, Yargıtay dosya inceleme sıra durumu).
- Over the sub-class 'file at chamber for <2 months, of which 6 weeks were judicial recess': no published rate found; the file would be at day ~62 on 17 Sep, day ~17 of available working time.
- No published base rate found for expedition of politically salient party-leadership files; searched, absent.

CALENDAR: new judicial year opened 1 Sep 2026. No Yargıtay bulletin cadence or scheduled session date for this file located — searched, absent.

EVIDENCE POINTING EARLIER: July reporting citing 'Yargıtay kaynakları' said the file would be taken up in September; the tetkik hakimi has had the file since late July, so it may be ripe for the panel from the first sitting; the case creates an acute leadership vacuum (Özel has left CHP and founded 'YENİ Parti'; ~49 CHP members are staying pending the ruling), which is a standing argument for expedited handling; the BAM decision itself arrived as a surprise with no pre-announcement.

EVIDENCE POINTING LATER: reporting dated 6 Sep 2026 states the cassation decision is anticipated 'by November', with the 49 dissident members planning to move only if no ruling comes by then (Türkiye, 6 Sep); CHP under Kılıçdaroğlu is sequencing provincial and district congresses first and convening the Grand Congress only after cassation finalization, a plan measured in weeks-to-months (CNN Türk, 6 Sep); July reporting also used 'sonbahar' (autumn) rather than a specific date; no agenda or hearing date has been published as of 7 Sep; a separate CHP congress criminal case at Ankara 26. Asliye Ceza is set for 16 Sep 2026 and is a distinct proceeding that may generate headlines easily confused with cassation action.

SEARCHED FOR, NOT FOUND: any Yargıtay agenda/heyet date for this file; any statement that the tetkik hakimi report is complete; any prediction market on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or a bookmaker covering this event (Polymarket has been blocked in Türkiye since 16 Jul 2026); any AA bulletin between 1-7 Sep 2026 reporting movement on the cassation file.

calls.reasoning: The appeal has been ripe at the Yargıtay 3rd Civil Chamber since ~July 17 but was frozen by the July 20-Aug 31 recess; only ~4 working days of the new judicial year have elapsed with no ruling and no announced agenda date. The reference class - a Turkish Yargıtay civil chamber merits ruling landing inside a specific ~10-day window when no date is scheduled and media consensus places the horizon months out - implies a low single-to-low-double-digit rate, and normal chamber disposition times run months. The strongest current evidence is Sept 6 reporting that insiders expect the decision 'by November', plus CHP-side calendars (Sept 9 congress-calendar announcement, Sept 18 leadership meeting) that all presuppose no ruling before Sept 18. Offsetting upward: extreme political salience, the tetkik hakimi report likely prepared during recess, and civil chambers deciding on the papers with no advance notice, so a ruling could drop any day; several July outlets did say the file would be taken up 'in September'. Offsetting downward further: the fine print excludes a finalization via appeal withdrawal or a ruling only on the CHP entity's Aug 25 feragat, both live non-merits paths. Media has already slipped this expectation once (July -> September -> autumn).

calls.reference_class: High-profile Turkish Yargitay civil-chamber appeals pending on the merits with no scheduled decision date, where reporting places the expected ruling 2+ months out - probability the merits ruling lands in a designated ~10-day window

calls.reasoning: Reference class: a specific ~10-day window inside a Yargiitay civil-chamber temyiz review with no announced agenda date, where reporting points to an autumn (Sept-Nov) horizon. Base rate from a roughly uniform hazard over Sept 7 - Nov 30 (85 days), times ~0.75 that a merits ruling lands by end-November at all, gives ~9%. Evidence for YES: the tetkik hakimi has had the file in preliminary examination since ~July 26, so the report is plausibly ready; cassation civil chambers decide on the papers and can issue with no public warning; there is political pressure from the Kilicdaroglu side, which cannot convene a Grand Congress until finalization. Evidence for NO: as of Sept 6 no agenda/decision date had been announced by the chamber; Turkish outlets consistently signal 'sonbahar'/November; CHP scheduled a leadership meeting for Sept 18 (one day after the deadline) and is sequencing provincial/district congresses first; the Aug 25 partial appeal withdrawals could produce a non-merits disposition, which the fine print explicitly excludes. Evidence is thin and one-sided toward delay, so I stay near the hazard-model base rate with only a small upward nudge for surprise-ruling risk. No market exists on this contract.

calls.reasoning: The file has been at Yargıtay 3. HD since 17-20 July but 6 of those 7 weeks were adli tatil; only ~4 working days of the new judicial year have elapsed and ~7 business days remain to the deadline. No agenda, hearing, or decision date has been announced. A roughly uniform hazard over the reported Sept-Nov horizon, discounted for the real chance the ruling slips past November, puts a 10-day window near 9%. I shade slightly below that: the most current insider reporting (6 Sep) says 'by November', the first post-recess week produced no movement, and both CHP-side calendars now on record — the 9 Sep congress-calendar announcement and the 18 Sep leadership meeting — presuppose no ruling before the deadline. Offsetting upward, civil chambers decide dosya üzerinden with zero notice and the tetkik hakimi report has been ripening since late July, so a ruling can drop on any working day. Additional NO drag from the fine print: a disposition confined to the 25 Aug withdrawals would not count.
calls.reconciliation: No web access on this run; reconciled on the three dossiers. Disputes: (1) identity of the 25 Aug withdrawing appellants — Run 1 names three individuals with the CHP HQ appeal still live, Run 2 says the CHP legal entity withdrew; unsettleable here, but immaterial because all three runs and the question background agree Özel's own temyiz remained on file, so the merits path stays open and the fine print bars a withdrawal-only disposition from counting. (2) Window size — Run 2's '~13 business days' is wrong for Sept 7-17; Runs 1/3 give ~7-8, which is arithmetically correct and is what I used. (3) Whether the tetkik hakimi report is complete — all three searched and failed to confirm; left as genuine uncertainty and it is the main channel for an unannounced ruling. (4) Pure judgment: how hard to lean on the 6 Sep 'by November' reporting. No evidence breaks this tie, so I take the reading I would bet on — it is expectation reporting, not a court statement, but every prior slippage on this file has been later rather than earlier, and it is corroborated by two independent CHP-side calendars built around no imminent ruling. I adopt Run 3's hazard construction as the anchor and shade modestly below it for the barren first post-recess week and the excluded non-merits paths, landing at 0.08 — inside the runs' range but below their centre, because the reconciled evidence is one-sided toward delay. Market check: all three runs independently searched Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi and bookmakers and found no contract; the harness title search also found none. No crowd anchor exists.
